name: tutorial
description: Plays Tutorial Pit start to finish using only controls a player can click. No console command stands in for a player action — if a step cannot be completed by clicking, this fails and names the control that blocked.

beats.goal: start the tutorial from a fresh Tutorial Pit
raise the game speed with the speed button
open the Crew panel and hire a surveyor

expect.note: The tutorial is on rails: leaving for the world map mid-step is how a player loses it, so that button must be inert while the tutorial is up.

beats.goal: the hired surveyor can actually be sent to survey

expect.note: A surveyor who cannot survey is not a surveyor. If Run is disabled here, hiring grants no geology qualification and no button in the game grants one.

beats.goal: run a survey and let the surveyor complete it

actions.note: the default ground-level camera already shows tile (23,23), but at that framing its own screen position falls directly under the placement strip's RESULT block, which catches clicks across its whole bar; a real player would look at the spot before clicking it, which is what this does

beats.goal: hire a driller
dig the box cut so the first blast has a face to break toward

expect.note: Open pits start with an access cut dug before the first shot: blasted rock swells and needs a void to fall into. The cut runs down the west side of the drill pattern, so the blast that follows breaks toward a free face instead of cracking flat ground in place.

beats.goal: the grid tool refuses a rectangle that is not the one asked for

expect.note: Inside the outlined square but not equal to it. The tutorial asks for exact coordinates, so Confirm must stay dead — otherwise the step teaches one layout and accepts another.

beats.goal: lay out the drill grid on the exact coordinates asked for

actions.note: centres the camera on the 10x10 rectangle's midpoint, clear of the placement strip's docked bar, before dragging its corners

beats.goal: charge every hole
sequence the detonation delays
fire the blast and confirm it

expect.note: Close dismisses BlastReportModal, which auto-opens with the real report right after DETONATE; scores step auto-advances, so the tutorial step is checked in the next beat

beats.goal: answer the scripted consultant event
hire a manager
accept a contract
hire a driver
buy a hauler and put the hired driver in it

expect.note: Deliberately does NOT force ticks (letTimePass) and does NOT touch the speed control. Forcing ticks bypasses the held clock and masks the deadlock this beat catches; cranking the speed burns the step tick budget before the driver starts walking, which holds the clock and freezes the driver — the same deadlock from the other side. The beat just waits: assigning a driver sends them walking, and the tutorial's own clock (kept live because a walk is work-in-progress) carries them to the vehicle. The timeout is large because a GPU-less environment renders frames slowly, so the handful of ticks the walk needs take real wall-clock time to accrue.

beats.goal: place a freight warehouse

actions.note: the camera is still framed on the blast site from the earlier steps — the warehouse region sits on the opposite side of the map, so it needs to actually be on screen before it can be clicked

beats.goal: haul the blasted debris into the warehouse with the Vehicles panel's Haul button

expect.note: The reported bug: no UI control anywhere could trigger `vehicle haul`, so this is where a real player got stuck forever.

beats.goal: deliver against the contract accepted earlier

expect.note: finances and needs cards auto-advance; set-policy is asserted next

beats.goal: change the site policy from Operations

expect.note: Deliberately presses Apply without touching a control first. The form mirrors the policy already in force, so this is the path a player takes — and it used to leave the step stuck while the panel said the policy had been updated.

beats.goal: let time run so production ticks over

expect.note: The last thing the tutorial asks of the player is to let time run, so reaching the closing cards is the end of the guided path. Either is a correct outcome: victory hands off to the completion card as soon as the level's profit target is met, and whether that happens within these ticks is campaign economy rather than playability.
